How the comment system works:
(as it will when it is complete, but 90% of this is accurate)

Comments load only if you scroll down. Each comment can only be voted up to prevent downvote censoring. If you don't like what someone says, say something more intelligent, more correct. This encourages rational discussion and also forces people to see what they don't like. This is a good thing.

Each comment can have up to four sub-comments and a page can have a comment depth of four. You can always still comment though.

The exception is applied to videos themselves which can have more.

Replying to a comment that has four or more children will slide one comment off. Comments like youtube are not permanent. Removal is probabilistic and inversely proportional to comment score. This leaves the important things to say up on the page.

If you comment or vote while not logged in a modal will log you in or register you and perform the vote or comment submission at the same time. This is all done without reloading the page.

There are no restrictions on comment depth currently.

There's a lot of applicable tech between the two ventures, and as IIRC; neither Tesla or SpaceX really patent anything (that way it doesn't get stolen and immediately utilized by China or other players) so there's likely a lot of lateral transfer of skills and knowledge.

Think of the SpaceX ships: If Musk wants to scale up to use mass production (which they will likely need for many of the crew capsules for their mars program) they can use the technologies and expertise in Tesla to streamline this process. Technology on Mars will be entirely reliant on solar capture and battery storage, something Tesla is pioneering right now and creating entirely in-house with their gigafactory.

Algorithms for self driving or assisted driving in cars can likely be utilized in some facet as a backbone for self maneuvering for space capsules making docking far easier. Even if they can't be transferred having staff in house that have knowledge of the base code and requirements has to be translatable.

Knowledge of government subsidies probably blend both with SpaceX and Tesla reducing lobbying costs. Being able to sell Teslas is essentially offboarding a portion of the costs from the necessity of developing both an infrastructure for material production, R&D and institutional knowledge.
